newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senator urges France to return stolen art.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator urges France to return stolen art.

text.p: U.S. Sen. Alfonse D'Amato urged France on Thursday to return almost 2,000 works of art in French museums he said were stolen by the Nazis from Holocaust victims.

"It is time for justice for the victims of the Holocaust. The Nazis stole their money, they stole their gold, they took their teeth and they took their art. It is an outrage," D'Amato, a New York Republican, said in a Senate speech.
As he spoke, D'Amato displayed a copy of the painting "The Cliffs of Etretat After the Storm" by Gustave Courbet, which he said was one of those stolen.
"This painting sits today the Musee D'Orsay and the simple truth is that it does not belong to them. This is unconscionable," D'Amato said.
In a letter to the French ambassador in Washington, D'Amato asked for a list of 1,995 pieces of artwork looted by the Nazis now in storage in Paris.
He also asked for information about what steps France was taking to identify the rightful owners of the artwork and of dormant bank accounts in French banks of Holocaust victims.
He called for an independent party to determine the rightful owners and return the art works to them.
D'Amato, as chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, has been leading an investigation of assets of Holocaust victims held by Swiss banks.
